steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Destructive testing damages or destroys the test specimen: tensile testing, impact testing, fatigue testing and hardness testing.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Non-destructive testing (NDT) evaluates components without damage: visual inspection, ultrasonic, X-ray, dye penetrant and magnetic particle testing.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Tensile testing stretches a specimen to failure, measuring yield strength, UTS, ductility (elongation) and elastic modulus.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Hardness testing presses an indenter into the surface: Brinell (ball), Vickers (diamond pyramid), Rockwell (ball or cone).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Distinguish clearly between destructive (specimen damaged) and non-destructive (component intact) testing. In tensile test questions, identify the key points on the stress-strain curve: elastic limit, yield point, UTS, fracture. NDT questions: name the specific method AND explain what type of defect it detects (surface vs internal). Tolerance questions: state the maximum and minimum acceptable values explicitly. Quality control vs quality assurance: QC checks the product; QA ensures the process is correct.
